author: Isidorus Hispalensis

passages.original: Et ideo si quid in hoc displicuerit, sibi imputet, quae tantum amat, ut timorem tollat. Nam perfecta charitas foras mittit timorem. Speciali quoque gratia fretus speciali domino, in quo vires sanctae Ecclesiae consistunt, suggero ut, quia Eusebius noster metropolitanus decessit, habeas misericordiæ curam. Et hoc filio tuo nostro domino suggeras, ut utilem illi loco præficiat, cujus doctrina I et sanctitas cnteris sit vitæ forma. Hunc autem filium præpsentem beatissimae potestati vestrae per omnia commendo, et tam de his quæ hic suggessimus , quam etiam de his quae supra questi sumus, eloquio vestro per eum illustrari mereamur.
passages.english: And so, if anything in this has given displeasure, let it lay the blame on itself, since it loves so much that it takes away fear. For perfect love casts out fear. Relying also on a special grace, I suggest to a special lord, in whom the strength of the holy Church rests, that, since our metropolitan Eusebius has died, you take care to show mercy. And suggest this to your son, our lord, that he set over that see a useful man, whose teaching and holiness may be a pattern of life for the others. This son, the bearer of this letter, I commend in every respect to your most blessed power; and may we be found worthy to be enlightened by your words through him, both about the things we have suggested here and about those we complained of above.
passages.notes: "sibi imputet, quae tantum amat": the subject is evidently the 'grace of your benevolence' (gratia) from the preceding sentence. Scanning errors corrected: "cnteris" read as "ceteris", "præpsentem" as "præsentem"; the stray "I" after "doctrina" is omitted. "filio tuo nostro domino" presumably refers to a king; it is not identified in the text. "illi loco" is taken as the vacant metropolitan see.
